expectations.text: Recommends the small consensus committee model for this pool, given 190 proposals, six readers and one synchronous discussion round
expectations.evidence: Four graders plus two non-voting anonymizers, one synchronous call, 'Solo curation is off the table.'

expectations.text: Replaces the proposed 1-to-5 quality average with the letter-grade advocate scale (A/B/C/D/X), whose grades describe advocacy rather than quality
expectations.evidence: 'A/B/C/D/X advocacy grade, plus a mandatory comment'

expectations.text: States that A means the reviewer will actively advocate, B means likes it but will not advocate, C means neutral, and D means will advocate against
expectations.evidence: A 'I will actively advocate'; B 'I like it and won't advocate'; C Neutral; D 'I will argue against it'

expectations.text: Includes an X grade meaning the reviewer abstains because they suspect they have identified the speaker
expectations.evidence: 'X | Abstain: I think I know the speaker, or I have a close tie'

expectations.text: States that grades aggregate as a best-worst pair per proposal (for example 'AC') and are never averaged
expectations.evidence: 'Best-worst pair per proposal (e.g. "AC"). Never an average.'

expectations.text: States that at least one A is the practical floor for serious consideration, so a proposal carrying only B, C and D grades cannot get in
expectations.evidence: 'Zero A grades: out, unless a grader asks on the call to rescue it.' The rescue clause lets a no-A proposal in.

expectations.text: Requires a written comment attached to every grade
expectations.evidence: 'Mandatory, 1–3 sentences. A grade without a reason is incomplete.'

expectations.text: Instructs writing the rubric down before any scoring begins, and warns that changing the rules once scoring has opened invalidates what was already read
expectations.evidence: 'Committee signs off the rubric... No grading before this.' It never warns that changing rules after scoring invalidates earlier reads.

expectations.text: States that the cut rule, as a threshold or a percentage, must be fixed before anyone sees the ranking
expectations.evidence: 'Cut rule (write it down before anyone scores)'; 'tighten before looking at who is in the set'

expectations.text: Runs the topic, employer and first-timer balance pass on the shortlist rather than on all 190 proposals
expectations.evidence: 'Program-fit pass (shortlist only, 15 minutes)'

expectations.text: Recommends an explicitly ordered backup list, cites about five talks as the documented single-track size, and flags any other number as extrapolation
expectations.evidence: 'ordered backup list of about 5 talks. Five is one documented single-track size, not a rule.'

expectations.text: Does not recommend averaging numeric scores or ranking proposals by mean score
expectations.evidence: 'Never an average'; rule-based cut on grades

expectations.text: Recommends the small consensus committee model for this pool, given 190 proposals, six readers and one synchronous discussion round
expectations.evidence: Recommends a per-rater numeric sheet with two passes and a script merge, not a small consensus committee.

expectations.text: Replaces the proposed 1-to-5 quality average with the letter-grade advocate scale (A/B/C/D/X), whose grades describe advocacy rather than quality
expectations.evidence: Keeps 'Fit 1-5', 'Substance 1-5', 'Clarity 1-5' columns.

expectations.text: States that A means the reviewer will actively advocate, B means likes it but will not advocate, C means neutral, and D means will advocate against
expectations.evidence: No advocacy grades defined; only a 1-5 anchor legend.

expectations.text: Includes an X grade meaning the reviewer abstains because they suspect they have identified the speaker
expectations.evidence: Uses a COI column with No/Suspect/Know instead of an X grade.

expectations.text: States that grades aggregate as a best-worst pair per proposal (for example 'AC') and are never averaged
expectations.evidence: 'score = mean(Fit, Substance, Clarity)' and z-scores.

expectations.text: States that at least one A is the practical floor for serious consideration, so a proposal carrying only B, C and D grades cannot get in
expectations.evidence: No such rule appears.

expectations.text: Requires a written comment attached to every grade
expectations.evidence: 'Required for any Y or N or any 1 or 5.' Comments are not required on every grade.

expectations.text: Instructs writing the rubric down before any scoring begins, and warns that changing the rules once scoring has opened invalidates what was already read
expectations.evidence: Only 'Decide the weights now, before anyone sees results.' No warning that changing rules invalidates scoring already done.

expectations.text: States that the cut rule, as a threshold or a percentage, must be fixed before anyone sees the ranking
expectations.evidence: Weights are fixed in advance but the cut rule is not; the cut is set by band and discussion.

expectations.text: Runs the topic, employer and first-timer balance pass on the shortlist rather than on all 190 proposals
expectations.evidence: A duplicate-speaker and same-company check runs by script on all proposals; the balance check comes late in the call but is not scoped to a shortlist.

expectations.text: Recommends an explicitly ordered backup list, cites about five talks as the documented single-track size, and flags any other number as extrapolation
